```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

set.seed(12)

library(RKaggle)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(car)
library(lmtest)
library(olsrr)

library(DT)
library(glmnet)
library(tibble)
library(forcats)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(corrplot)
library(mice)
```

## **DATA COLLECTION**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
data <- read.csv("../Video_Games_Sales_as_at_22_Dec_2016.csv",sep=",",na.strings=c(""," ","NA","N/A"))

data_row_count <- nrow(data)
```

#### Number of rows = **`r data_row_count`**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Show data
datatable(data[1:6,], 
          options = list(scrollX = TRUE, pageLength = 6),
          rownames = FALSE)
```

## **DATA CLEANSING**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Drop all sales except global
data_df <- cbind(data[,-c(6:10)],data$Global_Sales)
data_df$Year_of_Release <- 2016 - data_df$Year_of_Release
names(data_df)[3] <- "Game_Age"
names(data_df)[12] <- "Global_Sales"

str(data_df)

summary(data_df)
```

## **DATA IMPUTATION**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
data_subset <- data_df[, c("Global_Sales", "Platform", "Game_Age", "Genre", "Critic_Score", "Critic_Count", "User_Count", "Rating")]

data_subset$Platform <- as.factor(data_subset$Platform)
data_subset$Genre <- as.factor(data_subset$Genre)
data_subset$Rating <- as.factor(data_subset$Rating)

meth <- make.method(data_subset)

imp_norm <- mice(data_subset, method = "pmm", m = 1, seed = 123, printFlag = FALSE)

completed_data <- complete(imp_norm, 1)

datatable(completed_data, 
          options = list(scrollX = TRUE, pageLength = 6),
          rownames = FALSE)
```

## **REGRESSION MODEL**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
set.seed(12)

reg_model <- completed_data
str(reg_model)

# 70 : 30 RATIO
train.size <- floor(0.7*nrow(reg_model))
train.index <- sample(1:nrow(reg_model),train.size, replace = F)
train.set <- reg_model[train.index,]
test.set <- reg_model[-train.index,]
```

Train Size: **`r nrow(train.set)`**

Test Size: **`r nrow(test.set)`**

Total Size: **`r nrow(data)`**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
model <- lm(formula = Global_Sales ~ Platform + Game_Age + Genre + Critic_Score + Critic_Count + User_Count + Rating, data = completed_data)
summary(model)

model$coefficients
```

## **OUTLIERS, LEVERAGE AND INFLUENTIAL POINTS**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
which(hatvalues(model) > 0.08)
plot(hatvalues(model),type="h"); abline(h=0.08)
which(cooks.distance(model)>1)
plot(cooks.distance(model),type="h"); abline(h=1)
```

## **DIAGNOSTIC CHECKING**

### **I. NORMALITY**

#### **1. Graphical Analysis of Residuals**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
qqnorm(residuals(model), ylab="Residuals")
qqline(residuals(model)) # Normality using Q-Q Plots
```

#### **2. Statistical Test**

**Ho**: ϵ’s normally distributed.

**Ha**: ϵ’s not normally distributed.

##### **2.1. Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
resid_std <- scale(residuals(model)) # mean=0, sd=1
ks_test <- ks.test(resid_std, "pnorm") # Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test
ks_test
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
p_value = ks_test$p.value
```

`r if(p_value >= 0.05) { "We fail to reject the null hypothesis, therefore, **the residuals are normally distributed.**" } else { "We reject the null hypothesis, therefore, **the residuals are not normally distributed.**" }`

### **II. HOMOSCEDASTICITY**

#### **1. Graphical Analysis of Residuals**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
plot(fitted(model), residuals(model))
```

#### **2. Statistical Test**

**Ho**: Heteroscedasticity is not present.

**Ha**: Heteroscedasticity is present.

##### **2.1. Breusch-Pagan-Godfrey Test**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
bp_test <- bptest(model) # Breusch-Pagan test
bp_test
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
p_value <- bp_test$p.value
```

`r if(p_value >= 0.05) { "We fail to reject the null hypothesis, therefore, **Heteroscedasticity is not present.**" } else { "We reject the null hypothesis, therefore, **Heteroscedasticity is present.**" }`

### **III. MULTICOLINEARITY**

#### **1. Statistical Test**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
vif_values = vif(model)
vif_values
```

VIF > 5 -> **moderate concern**

VIF > 10 -> **serious multicollinearity**

```{r, echo=FALSE}
check_col <- vif_values[, ncol(vif_values)]

for (i in 1:length(check_col)) {
  var_name <- names(check_col)[i]
  val <- check_col[i]
  
  if (val > 5) {
    print(paste("WARNING:", var_name, "has moderate multicollinearity (VIF =", round(val, 2), ")"))
  } else if (val > 10) {
    print(paste("WARNING:", var_name, "has high multicollinearity (VIF =", round(val, 2), ")"))
  } else {
    print(paste(var_name, "is okay (VIF =", round(val, 2), ")"))
  }
}
```

### **IV. INDEPENDENCE**

#### **1. Graphical Analysis of Residuals**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
n = length(residuals(model))
plot(tail(residuals(model), n-1) ~
head(residuals(model), n-1),
xlab=expression(hat(epsilon)[i]),
ylab=expression(hat(epsilon)[i+1]))
abline(h=0, v=0, col = grey(0.5))
```

#### **2. Statistical Test**

**Ho**: No auto-correlation (the errors are uncorrelated)

**Ha**: There exists auto-correlation

##### **2.1. Durbin-Watson Test**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
dw_test = dwtest(model) # Durbin-Watson Test
dw_test
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
p_value <- dw_test$p.value
```

`r if(p_value >= 0.05) { "We fail to reject the null hypothesis, therefore, **there is no auto-correlation.**" } else { "We reject the null hypothesis, therefore, **there exists auto-correlation.**" }`

## DATA Transformation

Since the model is not normally distributed based on the results of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, we perform a data transformation using the **Logarithmic Model**.

```{r, warning=FALSE}
train.set$Log_Global_Sales <- log(train.set$Global_Sales)

model_log <- lm(Log_Global_Sales ~ Platform + Game_Age + Genre + 
                Critic_Score + Critic_Count + User_Count + Rating, 
                data = train.set)

summary(model_log)
```

## **OUTLIERS, LEVERAGE AND INFLUENTIAL POINTS**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
which(hatvalues(model_log) > 0.08)
plot(hatvalues(model_log),type="h"); abline(h=0.08)
which(cooks.distance(model_log)>1)
plot(cooks.distance(model_log),type="h"); abline(h=1)
```


```{r, warning=FALSE}
ks_test
```

```{r, include=FALSE}

```

`r if(p_value >= 0.05) { "We fail to reject the null hypothesis, therefore, **the residuals are normally distributed.**" } else { "We reject the null hypothesis, therefore, **the residuals are not normally distributed.**" }`

### **II. HOMOSCEDASTICITY**

#### **1. Graphical Analysis of Residuals**


`r if(p_value >= 0.05) { "We fail to reject the null hypothesis, therefore, **Heteroscedasticity is not present.**" } else { "We reject the null hypothesis, therefore, **Heteroscedasticity is present.**" }`

### **III. MULTICOLINEARITY**

#### **1. Statistical Test**


```{r, warning=FALSE}
k
```
